reading.body:
Alteryx provides analytics automation software that integrates AI for data blending and self-service analytics, positioning itself in the data preparation layer rather than model development or inference.

The distinction matters for AI infrastructure. Data quality and preparation consume significant engineering effort before any model sees input, yet the compute requirements here are modest compared to training or deployment. Alteryx sits upstream of the inference path, automating the human work of structuring raw data into usable form. This belongs to the broader stack, but it is not where compute constraints tighten.

The data covers a single product line and does not specify deployment scale, customer base, infrastructure needs, or power consumption. It identifies what Alteryx does, not the resource requirements that would connect it to the binding constraints on AI scaling. The category label "Data & Analytics AI" is broad enough that the actual role in any particular AI project—whether critical or peripheral—remains unclear from this entry alone.

profile_text.body:
Alteryx is a data analytics and automation company that describes itself as the agentic analytics and automation company. Its site says it helps organizations turn complex data into trusted insights, decisions, and action through AI-ready datasets, governed business logic, and visual workflows. The company was founded in 2011 and is headquartered in Irvine. Its main offering described on the site is Alteryx One, which the company says automates data workflows, reduces manual work, and delivers insights faster, and which it says integrates with Snowflake, Databricks, and business intelligence tools.

On AI, Alteryx positions its platform around trust and governance rather than model development. The site says every workflow Alteryx One produces is visible, understandable, repeatable, and auditable, and that agents created by the platform inherit the same properties. It also says business teams can embed their own rules and judgment into governed, automated workflows while IT retains guardrails. The company says it is rated a leader across multiple 2026 analyst evaluations, and it cites McLaren Racing as using Alteryx AI data analytics to analyze data on and off the track. Alteryx also promotes events featuring CEO Andy MacMillan, MIT's Dr. Barb Wixom, Steve Nouri, Nezrin Noushad, and Anthony Alteirac.

The product tracked here is Alteryx AI, listed under data and analytics AI, described as analytics automation with AI, data blending, workflow governance, and self-service analytics risk. No lawsuits or MCP server presence are recorded for the company.
